tasks.title: W1: per-load historical budget cap with oldest-first floor fill across loads
tasks.description: Cap what a single chart load may spend (at most floor(MAX_HISTORICAL_PER_600S/4) historical requests before yielding) and fill the 30-session depth floor monotonically oldest-first across successive loads, resuming from persisted state instead of restarting one giant wave (S-P7-1; code side of ESC-075/079).
acceptance_criteria: Given a rolling historical budget of B=MAX_HISTORICAL_PER_600S slots, when a 1-min chart load plans its backfill, then it issues at most floor(B/4) historical requests before yielding (the remainder stays queued for later loads).

Given a cache short of the AC-D16.8 30-session floor, when successive loads complete, then cached depth grows monotonically oldest-first across the loads and converges to the floor without any single wave carrying it all.

Given the capped planner in place, when the existing planner/backfill suites run, then find_missing_spans/plan_requests/floor_bar_budget semantics are unchanged (pure, Qt-free) and the scoped existing suites stay green.

tests.description: Drive load planning for SPY 1-min on an empty cache through a fake transport that counts req_historical_data issues; assert issued-before-yield <= floor(MAX_HISTORICAL_PER_600S/4).
tests.expected_result: Issued count is <= 25 at B=100 (and scales with the tunable, never a hardcoded 25); the leftover plans remain queued, not dropped.

tests.description: Complete two successive capped loads against a session/BarCache double; assert the second load starts from the first load's persisted depth, fills the next-oldest span first, and total cached sessions strictly increase toward the floor.
tests.expected_result: Depth after load 2 > depth after load 1 (monotonic, oldest-first); no re-request of already-persisted spans.

tests.description: Run the scoped existing suites (test_backfill_service, test_history_backfill*, test_d42_depth_floor, test_d42_day_presence) unmodified.
tests.expected_result: All scoped suites pass; no planner contract signature changed.

expected_artifacts: tests/test_p7_w1_cap.py (new: cap counting, cross-load monotonic fill)
outputs: Capped per-load wave; cross-load floor resume

tasks.title: W1: persist-and-render per chunk with resume-not-restart finalisation
tasks.description: Replace the all-or-nothing wave finalise with per-chunk save_bars persist plus incremental render on every completed chunk, so killing or reloading mid-wave loses zero fetched bars and overlapping resumes never duplicate rows (S-P7-2; code side of ESC-075).
acceptance_criteria: Given a wave with N chunks in flight, when any single chunk's historical_data_end arrives, then its bars are BarCache.save_bars-persisted and rendered before the remaining chunks complete (cache and chart advance monotonically per chunk, never only at the last chunk).

Given an interrupted wave (cancel, reload, or strand) that had completed K chunks, when the next load for the same target runs, then the K chunks' bars are still in the cache and on the chart (the cache after interruption is never smaller than before the wave started).

Given an overlapping resume that re-fetches already-persisted bars, when the duplicate bars arrive, then INSERT OR REPLACE idempotence yields no duplicate rows and exactly one save plus one set per completed chunk occurs (never per bar), with the generation fence still suppressing superseded waves.

tests.description: Drive a 3-chunk wave through the real TickerSession/MainWindow path with a fake transport; after each chunk-end assert BarCache row count grew and the chart/session bars include the new chunk while other chunks are still in flight.
tests.expected_result: Cache and rendered bars advance after chunk 1 and chunk 2, not only after chunk 3; per-chunk save+set observed exactly once per chunk.

tests.description: Interrupt a wave mid-flight (cancel/reload), then reload the same symbol/timeframe/mode and assert the previously completed chunks survive in cache and chart.
tests.expected_result: Post-interruption cache row count >= pre-wave count and includes the completed chunks; no refetch of completed spans.

tests.description: Feed the same chunk twice (overlap) and assert row counts, plus count save/set calls per chunk completion.
tests.expected_result: No duplicate (symbol,timeframe,ts) rows; one save plus one set per completed chunk; superseded-generation bars still rejected.

inputs: Capped per-load wave from P7-T01; BarCache idempotence

tasks.title: W1: same-chart reload coalescing, cancel-slot refund, superseded-162 at debug
tasks.description: Stop the cancel-and-respend storm: a reload that does not change symbol/timeframe/mode coalesces into the running wave, genuinely cancelled slots are refunded only when their request never reached TWS, and a 162 acknowledgement for a superseded reqId is debug-level instead of a user-facing error (S-P7-2; code side of ESC-076).
acceptance_criteria: Given an in-flight wave for a (symbol, timeframe, ext-hours) triple, when load_chart is called with the identical triple, then no tracked reqId is cancelled, the history generation is unchanged, and the wave continues (zero re-spend for data already in flight).

Given an in-flight wave, when load_chart is called with a different symbol, timeframe, or ext-hours mode, then the old wave cancels with a generation advance exactly as before (genuine target changes still fence off stale responses).

Given a cancelled reqId, when its request never reached TWS (pre-issue cancel), then its rolling-budget slot is refunded via the pacing owner; when the request was already issued (post-issue cancel), then its slot is kept (never refunded).

Given error 162 arriving for a cancel-tagged (superseded) reqId, when error ingress routes it, then it is logged at debug with no status-bar error; given 162 on a reqId this client did not cancel, when it arrives, then the existing warning plus status-bar plus retry path is unchanged.

tests.description: Start a wave, reload the identical triple mid-wave with a recording transport, and assert no cancel_historical_data call, unchanged generation, and continued chunk completion.
tests.expected_result: Zero cancels on identical reload; wave completes with the original reqIds; no duplicate spend.

tests.description: Start a wave, load a different symbol, and assert the old wave cancelled with a generation bump and stale responses rejected.
tests.expected_result: Old reqIds cancelled, generation advanced, late bars for the old reqIds ignored.

tests.description: Cancel one pre-issue reqId and one post-issue reqId; assert pacing slot counts via historical_wait_seconds/record state.
tests.expected_result: Pre-issue cancel frees exactly its slot; post-issue cancel frees nothing.

tests.description: Deliver 162 for a superseded reqId and for a live wave reqId; assert log-level and status-bar routing for each.
tests.expected_result: Superseded 162 is debug-only with no status-bar error; genuine 162 keeps warning plus status-bar plus retry.

outputs: Coalesced reloads; refund rule; quiet superseded-162

tasks.title: W2: watchdog bound covers pacing deferrals and strands cannot resume
tasks.description: Make the stranded-wave watchdog coherent with pacing: its bound is never below the scheduled continuation delay plus margin, and a strand finalise stops the continuation timer and clears the plan queue so a finalised wave can never resume or finalise twice (S-P7-3; code side of ESC-077).
acceptance_criteria: Given a wave legitimately waiting on a pacing deferral with continuation delay W, when the watchdog is armed, then its bound is at least W plus margin, so the wave is never flagged stranded while waiting out a legal deferral of up to the full budget-window continuation.

Given a strand finalise (watchdog timeout or transport drop), when it runs, then the wave continuation timer is stopped and the plan queue is cleared, so no further chunk issues and no second finalise can occur afterwards.

tests.description: Schedule continuations with waits from ~1 s up to the full budget-window wait using a fake clock; arm the watchdog and advance time past the old fixed 120 s bound while still inside W+margin.
tests.expected_result: No strand fires while the wave is inside its legal deferral at any wait; a wait beyond the computed bound still strands exactly once.

tests.description: Force a strand (timeout/disconnect) with queued plans and an armed continuation timer; then advance timers and deliver a late end marker.
tests.expected_result: Timer stopped, queue empty, exactly one finalise; late markers and timer ticks after the strand change nothing.

tasks.title: W2: aggregator-prime precedence over the backfill wave
tasks.description: Give the D27.9 aggregator prime precedence when a full wave starts alongside it (the wave defers its continuation by exactly one HISTORICAL_MIN_INTERVAL_S or the prime holds an explicit reservation), and make a skipped prime a counted warning instead of the expected-case log line (S-P7-4; code side of ESC-078).
acceptance_criteria: Given a backfill wave starting alongside the D27.9 aggregator prime, when the wave would issue while the shared historical-interval gate is closed, then the wave defers its continuation by exactly one HISTORICAL_MIN_INTERVAL_S (or the prime holds an explicit reservation) and the prime issues instead of starving.

Given a prime that cannot issue even with precedence, when the live feed attaches fail-open, then a warning names the skipped prime and a counter records it, so a starved prime is visible rather than logged as the routine pacing-limited line.

tests.description: Start a multi-chunk wave and the prime together with a closed interval gate; assert the prime reqId issues and the wave continuation slips by exactly one interval.
tests.expected_result: Prime issued (no fail-open skip); wave continuation delayed by exactly HISTORICAL_MIN_INTERVAL_S; ordering preserved across repeated runs.

tests.description: Force the prime retry to also find the gate closed; attach fail-open and assert the warning plus counter.
tests.expected_result: Warning names the skipped prime for the symbol/timeframe; the skip counter increments; the existing one-retry/fail-open semantics are otherwise unchanged (D27.9 intact).

inputs: Wave lifecycle from P7-T03; D27.9 priming semantics
outputs: Prime precedence rule; counted skipped-prime warning

tasks.title: W3: wide-duration decision point with measured before/after and owner gate
tasks.description: Turn the single-shot probe win into an explicit decision: record measured before/after per timeframe, re-verify pacing with any wide request in place, and change a TIMEFRAME_CONFIG duration value only with an owner-approval record naming that timeframe — otherwise the chained-request path stands and the wave is still complete (S-P7-5). No automated live step: any live measurement runs only by the method the owner names.
acceptance_criteria: Given each candidate timeframe, when the measurement suites run offscreen, then requests-per-load, time-to-first-bar, time-to-current, and pacing-slot spend are recorded before and after the widened duration for that timeframe.

Given the owner-gated rule, when this wave lands without an owner-approval record naming a timeframe, then that timeframe's TIMEFRAME_CONFIG duration value is byte-identical to before; a value changes only with the approval record present and naming it.
Given a widened duration in place, when backfill waves issue through it, then the 0.5 s minimum interval and the rolling budget still gate every request and no pacing path blocks the GUI thread.

Given a wide request that returns short or empty, when finalisation runs, then the shortfall surfaces as a status-bar message (never a silent hole) and the planner rolls back to chained requests for the uncovered span.

tests.description: Run the before/after harness per candidate timeframe against the fake transport with recorded timings; emit the measurement record (requests/load, first-bar latency, current latency, slot spend).
tests.expected_result: A complete before/after record exists for every timeframe the wave claims to widen; numbers are measured, not asserted constants.

tests.description: Inspect the git diff on ibkr/market_data.py TIMEFRAME_CONFIG durations and the owner-approval record: every changed duration names its approval, and every unapproved timeframe is diff-clean.
tests.expected_result: No silent constants edit exists; an unapproved widening fails this check by construction.

tests.description: Issue waves through the widened duration with a pacing spy; assert interval/budget gating and non-blocking deferral.
tests.expected_result: Minimum-interval and rolling-budget gates hold; deferrals use PacingExceeded plus singleShot; no GUI-thread sleep on any path.

tests.description: Return short/empty on a wide request; assert the surfaced shortfall and the chained-request rollback covering the gap.
tests.expected_result: Status-bar shortfall names the uncovered span; rollback plans chain over it; no silent hole.

expected_artifacts: tests/test_p7_w3_wide.py (new: before/after harness, pacing re-verify, rollback); ibkr/market_data.py durations only with approval
inputs: Stable W1/W2 wave lifecycle; probe evidence

tasks.title: W4: streaming correctness close-out (reconnect replay, health/backoff, burst integrity)
tasks.description: Close out streaming without redesigning it: prove reconnect replays subscriptions with rebound reqIds and no duplicate bars, stream-health/backoff transitions hold, realtime-bars priming stays intact under a tick burst with no dropped or late aggregated bars, and W1-W3 changed none of it (S-P7-6).
acceptance_criteria: Given live subscriptions at disconnect, when the transport reconnects, then every subscription replays with a rebound reqId, stream health returns through its documented transitions, and no bar is duplicated or lost across the replay.

Given a tick burst against primed aggregators, when aggregated bars push, then every tick is accounted exactly once in order, the forming candle reflects primed history (D27.9 intact), and no bar arrives late or dropped.

Given every pacing path touched by W1-W3 (wave continuation, prime retry, watchlist deferral), when pacing binds, then each path defers via PacingExceeded plus QTimer.singleShot and none blocks the GUI thread.

tests.description: Subscribe, disconnect mid-stream, reconnect with a fake transport that records reqIds; assert replayed subscriptions, rebound ids, health transitions, and bar-set equality (no dupes, no loss).
tests.expected_result: All pre-drop subscriptions replayed exactly once with fresh reqIds; bar multiset identical across the drop; health reaches live only on first post-reconnect bar.

tests.description: Prime aggregators then inject an out-of-order/tight tick burst; assert push ordering, priming survival, and forming-candle content.
tests.expected_result: No dropped or late bars; forming candle equals primed history plus burst ticks in order.

tests.description: Source-plus-behavior assertion: scan the W1-W3 pacing paths for blocking sleeps and drive each binding path to observe deferral.
tests.expected_result: Zero blocking-sleep primitives on any pacing path; every binding path defers via PacingExceeded plus singleShot.
